import re
import traceback

try:
    GOOD = re.compile(r"(?P<GE>>=)|(?P<GT>>)|(?P<EQ>=)|(?P<IDENT>[A-Za-z_]\w*)|(?P<INT>\d+)|(?P<SKIP>\s+)")
    BAD  = re.compile(r"(?P<GT>>)|(?P<GE>>=)|(?P<EQ>=)|(?P<IDENT>[A-Za-z_]\w*)|(?P<INT>\d+)|(?P<SKIP>\s+)")
    for name, pat in (("GE first", GOOD), ("GT first", BAD)):
        print(name, [(m.lastgroup, m.group()) for m in pat.finditer("x >= 5") if m.lastgroup != "SKIP"])

    NOB = re.compile(r"(?P<KEYWORD>if|else|while)|(?P<IDENT>[A-Za-z_]\w*)|(?P<SKIP>\s+)")
    WB  = re.compile(r"(?P<KEYWORD>\b(?:if|else|while)\b)|(?P<IDENT>[A-Za-z_]\w*)|(?P<SKIP>\s+)")
    for name, pat in (("no \\b", NOB), ("with \\b", WB)):
        print(name, [(m.lastgroup, m.group()) for m in pat.finditer("iffy")])
except Exception as e:
    print(f"[tokens:order_priority] {e}")
    traceback.print_exc()
description: Compare placing >= before > versus > before >= on x >= 5, and compare keyword patterns with and without \b anchors on iffy.

steps.description: Line 5 defines `GOOD` with `(?P<GE>>=)` before `(?P<GT>>)`, and line 6 defines `BAD` with `(?P<GT>>)` before `(?P<GE>>=)`. Lines 7-8 run both patterns on `"x >= 5"` and print the non-whitespace `(m.lastgroup, m.group())` pairs.

Compare the first two branches of `GOOD` (line 5) and `BAD` (line 6). Python's `|` operator takes the first branch that matches at the current index. Thus, `(?P<GE>>=)` inside `BAD` is unreachable whenever `>` appears.

Line 10 defines `NOB` with unanchored `(?P<KEYWORD>if|else|while)` before `IDENT`, while line 11 defines `WB` with word-boundary anchors `\b(?:if|else|while)\b` before `IDENT`. Lines 12-13 run both on `"iffy"`.

steps.answer: `NOB` matches the prefix `'if'` as `('KEYWORD', 'if')` and the remaining `'fy'` as `('IDENT', 'fy')`. `WB`'s `\b` anchor rejects `'if'` inside `'iffy'` and lets `IDENT` match the whole word `[('IDENT', 'iffy')]`.
steps.question: When `pat.finditer("iffy")` runs on line 13, what token list does `NOB` (without `\b`) produce compared to `WB` (with `\b`)?

steps.description: At trace step 6 on line 8, `GOOD` scans `"x >= 5"` and emits `[('IDENT', 'x'), ('GE', '>='), ('INT', '5')]` before the loop switches to `BAD`.
